Rashi on Ketubot 68a:10:1.hebrew: הא באכילה ושתיה כו' - שמין הנכסים: אם עני הוא, נותנין לה כפי מה ששנינו באע"פ (לעיל כתובות דף סד:), במשרה את אשתו על ידי שליש; ואם הנכסים מרובים, הכל לפי הכבוד:
Rashi on Ketubot 68a:10:1.english: This [refers] to eating and drinking, etc. - They assess the estate: if he [the father] was poor, they give her according to what we learned in [the chapter] Af Al Pi (above, Ketubot 64b), regarding "one who provisions his wife through a third party"; and if the estate is large, everything is according to [their] dignity.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:12:1.english: Poor in mind - It is not in his mind to give her a wealthy [man's] dowry, rather a poor [man's] dowry.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:16:1.english: She takes one-tenth of the estate - And we do not assess [the mindset of] the father.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:16:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: לא קשיא, הא דאמידניה, הא דלא אמידניה - הא דאמר רבי עישור נכסים, בדלא אמידניה לאב, שלא גר בינינו ולא עמדנו על סוף דעתו אם וותרן אם קמצן:
Rashi on Ketubot 68a:16:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: This is not difficult; this [is] where we assessed him, that [is] where we did not assess him - That which Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] said, "one-tenth of the estate," [applies] where we did not assess the father — [that is,] where he did not live among us and we did not ascertain his true disposition, whether [he is] generous or miserly.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:17:1.english: So too, it is reasonable - That where we assessed him, Rabbi agrees that we assess according to the father.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:19:1.english: The first - We initially assume [this means the one] who comes first to marry.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:1:1.english: With silver telei or with gold telei - With white linen tablecloths or with colored silk [ones].

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:1:2.hebrew: היינו חוטאים - שאנו מעלימין עין מן העניים, אבל עכשיו הרמאים גורמים לנו:
Rashi on Ketubot 68a:1:2.english: We would be sinning - For we turn a blind eye to the poor, but now the swindlers cause [us to do so].

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:3:1.english: One who blinds his eye - [He] makes himself appear as though his eye is blind.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:3:2.english: [One who] crushes [mekapeach] his leg - [Making it appear] as if his leg is shrunken.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:4:1.hebrew: אין מחייבין אותו למכור כו' - רישא דמתניתין: "מי שיש לו מאתים זוז, לא יטול לקט, שכחה ופאה":
Rashi on Ketubot 68a:4:1.english: They do not require him to sell, etc. - The beginning of the Mishnah [states]: "Whoever has two hundred zuz may not take leket [gleanings], shikhchah [forgotten sheaves], or pe'ah [the corner of the field]."

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:4:2.english: They do not require him to sell, etc. - To complete two hundred zuz so that he will not take [charity].

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:6:1.hebrew: כאן קודם שיבוא לידי גיבוי - הא דתנן אין מחייבין, מעיקרא קאי: כשבא ליטול לקט, ולא היו לו מאתים זוז, ואם היה מוכר כלי תשמישו היה משיג למאתים זוז — אין מחייבין אותו למכור. והא דתנן מחייבין, לאחר שבא לידי גיבוי — לאחר שהביא עצמו לידי כך שבית דין גובין הימנו: כגון שהיה לו מאתים זוז ונטל לקט שכחה ופאה, ונודע שעשיר היה, ב"ד באין וגובין הימנו מה שנטל; ואם אין לו כדי לשלם, מוכר כלי תשמישו היקרים ומשתמש בפחותים:
Rashi on Ketubot 68a:6:1.english: Here, before he comes to [the point of] collection - That which we learned in the Mishnah, "[we] do not obligate [him]," refers to the outset: when he comes to take gleanings [leket], and he did not have two hundred zuz, and if he were to sell his household utensils he would reach two hundred zuz — [we] do not obligate him to sell [them]. And that which we learned in the Mishnah, "[we] obligate [him]," [refers to] after he comes to [the point of] collection — after he has brought himself to such a state that the court collects from him: for example, where he had two hundred zuz and took gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and corner-of-the-field produce [leket, shikh'chah, and pe'ah], and it became known that he was wealthy, the court comes and collects from him what he took; and if he does not have [enough] to pay, he sells his expensive utensils and uses inferior ones.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:6:2.english: To [the point of] collection - That the court collects from him.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:7:1.hebrew: מדעתה - רבותא קמ"ל, דאע"פ שנתרצית, אין מחילתה מחילה:
Rashi on Ketubot 68a:7:1.english: With her consent - [This] teaches us a novel point: that even though she consented, her waiver is not a [valid] waiver.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:7:2.english: What is fit to be given to her - One-tenth of the estate.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:8:1.english: If [he] married off - the father in his lifetime [married off] the first daughter.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:8:2.hebrew: ינתן כו' - בין שהוא עישור, בין שהוא פחות, בין שהוא יותר:
Rashi on Ketubot 68a:8:2.english: [It] should be given, etc. - Whether it is a tenth [of the property], whether it is less, [or] whether it is more.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:9:1.hebrew: לפרנסה שמין באב - הבת יתומה שבאת לינשא, נותנים לה נדוניא כפי אומד שאנו בקיאין באביה, וותרן או קמצן:
Rashi on Ketubot 68a:9:1.english: For support, we assess based on the father - [Regarding] an orphaned daughter who comes to marry, they give her a dowry according to an estimate based on our familiarity with her father — [whether he was] generous or stingy.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:9:2.english: Support of the husband - [The] dowry for marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 68a:9:3.english: Her own support - Sustenance while she is with [her] brothers.

Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:11:1.hebrew: אי נימא עני עני בנכסים כו' - והשתא אתי שמואל שפיר כרבנן, דרבנן נמי סברי דשמין באב. והכי קאמר: "פעמים שאדם עשיר בשעה שנתן לראשונה ועכשיו העני בנכסים" — ולא היה נותן לזאת כמו שנתן לראשונה, ולית לן למימר ינתן לשניה כדרך שנתן לראשונה — "אלא שמין את הנכסים", כלומר: ונותנין לפי מה שהיה נותן האב עכשיו מנכסים מועטים הללו, והיינו שמין באב. ופריך: "מכלל דת"ק סבר כו', הא לית ליה"? כלומר, לית ליה כמו שהיה לו מתחלה, ודאי הוא שלא נותן עכשיו כמו שנתן מתחלה, ובהא ודאי לא א"ר יהודה "ינתן לשניה כו'"; אלא לאו "עני" — עני בדעת, והשתא אין לפרש "שמין את הנכסים" שישומו באב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:11:1.english: If we say [that] "poor" [means] poor in property, etc. - And now Shmuel accords well with the Rabbis, for the Rabbis also hold that we appraise according to the father['s disposition]. And this is what [the Mishnah] is saying: "Sometimes a person is wealthy" at the time he gave to the first [daughter], "and now he has become poor in property" — so he would not give to this [second daughter] as he gave to the first, and we should not say that there should be given to the second [daughter] in the manner he gave to the first — "rather, we appraise the property," that is to say, and we give [her] according to what the father would give now from this diminished property; and this is [what Shmuel means by] "we appraise according to the father." And [the Gemara] asks: "By inference, the first tanna holds, etc. — but he does not have [it]!" That is to say, [since] he does not have as much as he had originally, it is certain that he would not give now as he gave originally, and in such a case Rabbi Yehudah certainly would not say, "Let there be given to the second [daughter], etc." Rather, is it not [that] "poor" [means] poor in disposition [i.e., stingy]? And now, "we appraise the property" cannot be explained [as meaning] that they appraise according to the father.

Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:1:1.hebrew: בטלי כסף או בטלי זהב - והא דלא עייפינהו ושדרינהו כמו מר עוקבא דלעיל, משום דבהנך דברים לא שייך פינוק, אלא ודאי עשיר היה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:1:1.english: Silver platters or gold platters - And [the reason] that [they] did not double [the coins] and send them, like Mar Ukva [did] above, is because with these things [the concept of] pampering does not apply; rather, he was certainly wealthy.

Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:1:2.hebrew: טלי זהב - מפה צבועה בתולעת שני, אדומה כזהב, דומיא דההיא דהשוכר את האומנין (ב"מ עח:):
Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:1:2.english: Gold cloths [telei zahav] - A cloth dyed with crimson [tola'at shani], red like gold, similar to that [case] in [the chapter] HaSokher Et HaUmanin (Bava Metzia 78b):

Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:4:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בפרנסת הבעל - קצת קשה לרשב"א, דהשתא לא הוי "שמין את הנכסים" דניזונת ומתפרנסת שוה; דלענין פרנסה הוי שמין את הנכסים לתת לה עישור נכסים, ולענין ניזונת שמין את הנכסים אם עני הוא, ונותנים כמו שמפורש באע"פ (לעיל כתובות דף סד:) במשרה אשתו על ידי שליש, ואם הנכסים מרובים — הכל לפי הכבוד:
Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:4:1.english: Is it not regarding provision by the husband? - This is somewhat difficult for Rashba, for now [the rule of] "we appraise the property" is not the same for "she is sustained" and "she is provided for"; for with respect to provision [dowry], "we appraise the property" means to give her one-tenth of the property, whereas with respect to sustenance, we appraise the property [to see] if he is poor, and they give [her] as is explained in [the chapter] Af Al Pi (above, Ketubot 64b) regarding one who provides for his wife through a trustee, and if the property is abundant — everything is according to [their] honor.

Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:4:2.hebrew: אי נימא עני עני בנכסים כו' - והשתא אתי שמואל שפיר כרבנן, דרבנן נמי סברי דשמין באב. והכי קאמר: פעמים שאדם עשיר בשעה שנתן לראשונה, ועכשיו העני בנכסים, ולא היה נותן לזאת כמו שנתן לראשונה, ולית לן למימר ינתן לשניה כדרך שנתן לראשונה, אלא שמין את הנכסים — כלומר, ונותנין לפי מה שהיה נותן האב עכשיו מנכסים מועטים הללו, והיינו שמין באב. ופריך: מכלל דת"ק סבר כו'. הא לית ליה — כלומר, לית ליה כמו שהיה לו מתחלה, ודאי הוא שלא נותן עכשיו כמו שנתן מתחלה, ובהא ודאי לא א"ר יהודה ינתן לשניה כו', אלא לאו עני עני בדעת, והשתא אין לפרש שמין את הנכסים שישומו באב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:4:2.english: If we say "poor" [means] poor in property, etc. - And now Shmuel accords well with the Rabbis, for the Rabbis also hold that we assess according to the father. And this is what [the Gemara] means: Sometimes a person is wealthy at the time he gave to the first [daughter], and now he has become poor in property, and he would not have given to this [second daughter] as much as he gave to the first; and we should not say, "let it be given to the second in the manner that he gave to the first," rather "we assess the property" — that is to say, we give according to what the father would give now from these limited properties, and that is [what is meant by] "we assess according to the father." And [the Gemara] challenges: This implies that the first Tanna holds, etc. "Behold, he does not have [it]" — that is to say, he does not have as much as he had at first; it is certain that he does not give now as much as he gave at first, and in this [case] Rabbi Yehudah certainly did not say, "let it be given to the second, etc." Rather, is it not [that] "poor" [means] poor in mind [i.e., stingy], and now "we assess the property" cannot be explained [to mean] that they assess according to the father.

Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:6:1.hebrew: כאן לאחר שבא לידי גיבוי - פי' בקונט' שנטל לקט שכחה ופאה, ונודע שהיה עשיר, ובאין בית דין לגבות מה שנטל. אף על גב דהוי ממון שאין לו תובעין, איכא למימר דמשום קנסא גובין ממנו; ואפילו את"ל בעלמא כהאי גוונא בבעל חוב מסדרין ואין מחייבין אותו למכור, הכא משום קנסא מחייבין אותו למכור. ור"ת פי': "קודם שיבא לידי גיבוי" — שאינו נוטל מקופה של צדקה, אלא מדברים שהם של הפקר, כגון לקט שכחה ופאה; ו"כאן לאחר שבא לידי גיבוי" — שנוטל מקופה של צדקה, מחייבין אותו למכור. וקשה קצת, דמשנה דאין מחייבין אותו למכור גבי לקט שכחה ופאה, ומשמע דברייתא נמי דמחייבת אותו למכור גבי לקט שכחה ופאה מתניא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:6:1.english: "Here, after he comes to collection" - Rashi explained that he took gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field, and it became known that he was wealthy, and the court comes to collect what he took. Even though it is money that has no [specific] claimants, one can say that because of a penalty they collect [it] from him; and even if you should say that elsewhere in a similar case regarding a creditor they make an assessment [of his basic needs] and do not obligate him to sell, here because of the penalty they obligate him to sell. And Rabbeinu Tam explained: "Before he comes to collection" [means] that he does not take from the charity fund, but rather from things that are ownerless, such as gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field; and "here, after he comes to collection" — [meaning] that he takes from the charity fund — they obligate him to sell. And [this] is somewhat difficult, for the Mishnah that [states] they do not obligate him to sell is [stated] regarding gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field, and it is implied that the Baraita as well, which obligates him to sell, is taught regarding gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field.

Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:9:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בפרנסת הבעל - קצת קשה לרשב"א, דהשתא לא הוי "שמין את הנכסים" דניזונת ומתפרנסת שוה; דלענין פרנסה הוי "שמין את הנכסים" לתת לה עישור נכסים, ולענין ניזונת שמין את הנכסים אם עני הוא ונותנים כמו שמפורש באע"פ (לעיל כתובות דף סד:) במשרה אשתו על ידי שליש, ואם הנכסים מרובים — הכל לפי הכבוד:
Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:9:1.english: "What, is it not [referring to] support for the husband?" - It is somewhat difficult for the Rashba, for now [according to this assumption], "appraising the property" with respect to "sustained" and "supported" is not the same: for with respect to support [for marriage], "appraising the property" means giving her a tenth of the property; whereas with respect to sustenance, they appraise the property [to see] if he is poor, and give [her] as is explained in [the chapter] Af Al Pi (above, Ketubot 64b) regarding one who provides for his wife through a trustee, and if the property is abundant, everything is according to [his] dignity.

Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:9:2.hebrew: לא בפרנסת עצמה - שאין שמין אותו באב, הואיל ועל כרחו מתחייב בתנאי בית דין; אבל פרנסת הבעל אין תלוי אלא בדעתו, כדאמרינן לקמן: "האומר אל יתפרנסו בנותיו מנכסיו — שומעין לו", ולכך שמין אותה באב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 68a:9:2.english: No, [it is referring] to her own support - For we do not evaluate it based on the father, since he is obligated [in it] against his will by a stipulation of the court; however, support [for] the husband [i.e., the dowry] depends only on his will, as we say later: "One who says, 'His daughters shall not be supported from his property' — we listen to him," and therefore we evaluate it based on the father.
